title: SceneAligner: 3D-Grounded Floorplan Localization in the Wild
claim: Our method turns unconstrained photo collections into 3D reconstructions aligned to a rasterized map, working on both exterior and interior large-scale scenes.
layout: 2 panels split by dashed line, left-to-right, colored image borders matched to cameras
description: Two side-by-side examples separated by a vertical dashed line, each reading left to right. Each example starts with a fan of in-the-wild photos with colored borders (cyan, orange, purple, pink). Next is a rasterized floorplan, then a black arrow, then a 3D point cloud with camera frustum icons. The frustums use the same colors as the photo borders, which links each image to its estimated camera pose. The left example is an exterior scene, a Hindu temple with a dark, blobby floorplan. The right example is an interior church scene with a long, thin, hand-drawn-style floorplan. In both, the reconstruction is a gravity-aligned point cloud sitting on top of the floorplan. Black frustums sit outside the floorplan footprint. The eye goes first to the colorful photo stacks, then to the large 3D reconstructions.
caption: Given a collection of in-the-wild images and a rasterized floorplan, SceneAligner reconstructs a gravity-aligned 3D point cloud from the images and globally aligns this reconstruction to the 2D floorplan map, thereby localizing the images within the floorplan. As illustrated above, our approach successfully aligns images capturing large-scale 3D environments, including exterior scenes (Doddabasappa Temple, left) and interior spaces (Église Saint-Martin d’Agonac, right).
abstract: Many public buildings provide floorplans with a "you are here" indicator to help visitors orient themselves. Floorplan localization seeks to computationally replicate this capability by determining where visual observations were captured within a floorplan. However, existing methods typically assume controlled small-scale environments and precise vectorized floorplans, limiting their ability to operate in large-scale buildings and rasterized floorplans. In this work, we present an approach for performing floorplan localization in the wild by grounding the task in a reconstructed 3D representation of the scene. Given an unconstrained image collection, our method reconstructs a gravity-aligned 3D scene and projects it into a 2D density map that serves as a floorplan proxy. Floorplan localization is then formulated as aligning this proxy with the input floorplan via a 2D similarity transform. To bridge the appearance gap between density maps and architectural floorplans, we adapt a 2D foundation model to learn cross-modal correspondences, introducing a fine-tuning scheme that encourages semantically aligned matches while preserving structural consistency. Extensive experiments demonstrate substantial improvements over prior methods, including in extremely sparse settings with as little as a single input image. Our code and data will be publicly available.
